recipes.title: Cheese Souffle
recipes.description: Souffles taste divine and they make an impressive presentation.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
Butter a 2-qrt souffle dish. Dust the bottom of the dish with the Parmesan cheese.
Use a saucepan to melt the butter. Add both flours. Mix vigorously.
While continuing to whisk, add the cream and water. Add the remaining Parmesan, the cheddar, and the salt and pepper.
Stir until mixture boils.
Take the saucepan off the stove and add the yolks. Whisk until integrated.
Pour the mixture in a bowl and let sit.
Beat the egg whites with a hand mixer for 5 minutes.
Fold the egg whites into the egg mixture.
Transfer the soufflé into the soufflé dish.
Bake for 40 minutes.

recipes.source_note: Reference cookbook - Quiche, Crepes and Souffles

recipes.title: Bacon and Double Cheese Quiche
recipes.source_note: Great American Home Baking (IMG_5631)
recipes.description: Paired with a tossed green salad, this full-flavored quiche makes an excellent lunch.

ingredients.item: chilled butter, cut into small pieces

instructions.text: To prepare the crust, in a large bowl, mix together the flour and salt. Using a pastry blender or 2 knives, cut in the butter until coarse crumbs form.
Add water, 1 tablespoon at a time, tossing with a fork, until a dough forms. Shape into a disk, wrap in plastic wrap, and chill in refrigerator for 30 minutes.

Preheat oven to 375°F. On a lightly floured surface, using a lightly floured rolling pin, roll the dough into 11-inch circle. Fit into 9-inch pie pan. Trim edge, leaving 1/2-inch overhang. Fold under to form standup edge. Prick dough with a fork. Line with foil and fill with pie weights or dried beans.
Bake for 10 minutes. Remove the foil and weights. Bake until lightly golden, about 5 minutes. Transfer to a wire rack to cool.
Meanwhile, prepare filling. In a medium skillet, cook the bacon over medium heat until crisp, 8 to 10 minutes. Transfer to a paper towel to drain.

In a small bowl, whisk together the eggs, cream, thyme, and pepper. Pour into crust. Crumble bacon. Sprinkle the egg mixture with the bacon, Gruyère cheese, and Cheddar cheese. Bake until golden and custard is set, about 30 minutes. Serve warm.

recipes.title: Shepherd's Cheese Bake
recipes.source_note: Cooking With The Ancients (IMG_6200)
recipes.description: A make-ahead breakfast casserole with bread layers and sharp cheese.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Remove crusts from bread and butter each slice. Butter a 2-quart casserole or deep baking dish.
Arrange a layer of bread slices on the bottom of the dish, cutting bread where necessary to fit.
Sprinkle bread layer with a layer of grated cheese. Repeat until all bread and cheese are used, ending with a layer of cheese.
Beat eggs, milk, and seasoning together. Pour over the contents of the baking dish.
Cover and store in the refrigerator overnight or for at least four hours. Sprinkle nutmeg over the top.
Bake uncovered for 40 minutes until puffed and golden brown.

notes: This dish should be assembled in advance, in the morning for the evening meal or the night before to be baked the next day.

recipes.title: Buckwheat Pancakes
recipes.source_note: Digital cookbook (Kindle)

instructions.text: Mix all ingredients together with a whisk.
Cook on a preheated lightly greased griddle or skillet.
Flip when bubbles begin to form on one side.
Serve hot with butter and warmed maple syrup.

recipes.title: Lemon Blueberry Pancakes
recipes.source_note: Digital cookbook (Kindle)

instructions.text: Preheat a pancake griddle.
Combine all ingredients in a large bowl.
Cook on the preheated griddle.
Serve hot with butter and warmed syrup.

recipes.title: Silver Dollars
recipes.source_note: Digital cookbook (Kindle)
recipes.description: Mini pancakes perfect for little hands.

instructions.text: Preheat a pancake griddle to high. Spray lightly with cooking spray.
Combine all ingredients in a large bowl.
Using a 1/4 cup measuring cup, drop batter onto griddle. Cook until batter begins to bubble and then flip to cook on the other side.
Serve immediately with soft butter and warmed syrup.

recipes.title: Cinnamon Spice Cakes
recipes.source_note: Digital cookbook (Kindle)

instructions.text: Preheat a pancake griddle.
Combine all ingredients in a large bowl.
Whisk together until well combined. Cook pancakes and serve hot with butter, warmed syrup and a sprinkle of powdered sugar if desired.

recipes.title: Banana Sour Cream Pancakes
recipes.source_note: Digital cookbook (Kindle)

instructions.text: Preheat a greased griddle to high.
Combine all ingredients, whisking to combine.
Cook pancakes, about 2 minutes on each side.
Serve hot with warmed syrup, butter, jam or peanut butter.

recipes.title: Cinnamon Chocolate Pancakes
recipes.source_note: Digital cookbook (Kindle)

instructions.text: Combine all ingredients and cook on a preheated greased griddle.
Serve immediately.

recipes.title: Toasted Pecan Blueberry Pancakes
recipes.source_note: Digital cookbook (Kindle)

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Toast the nuts by spreading them out on a lightly greased cookie sheet.
Melt the butter and cinnamon in the microwave and drizzle over pecans. Toast for about 10-15 minutes or until they lightly browned and crispy.
Combine flour, baking powder, salt, and sugar with a whisk.
Stir in the eggs, milk and oil.
Fold in the blueberries.
Drop pancake batter on griddle, about 1/4 cup for each pancake.
Top pancakes with toasted cinnamon pecans.

recipes.title: Blueberry Buckwheat Pancakes
recipes.source_note: Digital cookbook (Kindle)

instructions.text: Combine all ingredients and whisk together.
Cook on a hot griddle. Serve immediately.

recipes.title: Banana Blueberry Pancakes
recipes.source_note: Digital cookbook (Kindle)

instructions.text: Combine all ingredients and cook pancakes on a hot griddle.
Serve immediately.

recipes.title: Monkey Pancakes
recipes.source_note: Digital cookbook (Kindle)
recipes.description: Banana chocolate chip pancakes - a kid favorite!

instructions.text: Heat a large skillet or pancake griddle.
Combine ingredients with a whisk, folding in chocolate chips with a spatula.
Cook pancakes.
Drizzle tops of pancakes with honey, maple syrup and peanut butter.

recipes.title: Cornmeal and Berry Pancakes
recipes.source_note: Digital cookbook (Kindle)
recipes.description: Cornmeal pancakes served with honey butter and fresh berries.

instructions.text: Preheat a greased griddle.
In a medium bowl, mix the flour, cornmeal, salt and baking powder with a whisk.
In another bowl combine the eggs with the applesauce.
Add the oil and milk to the egg mixture.
Combine the wet ingredients into the dry.
Cook the pancakes on the griddle. In a small bowl, stir the honey and butter together.
Melt the honey butter in the microwave for 20 seconds or until melted and smooth.
Serve pancakes hot with honey butter and fresh berries.

recipes.title: Toasted Pecan Buttermilk Pancakes
recipes.source_note: Digital cookbook (Kindle)

instructions.text: Preheat an oven to 400°F.
Spread pecans out on a baking sheet.
Bake for about 10 minutes or until lightly toasted.
In a medium bowl, combine remaining ingredients.
Cook pancakes and serve hot with syrup, jam or peanut butter.

recipes.title: Autumn Spiced Pumpkin Pancakes
recipes.source_note: Digital cookbook (Kindle)
recipes.description: Whole wheat pancakes with warm fall spices, topped with apple butter.

instructions.text: Preheat a griddle with butter.
Combine the flours, baking powder, salt and spices in a medium bowl.
Whisk in the eggs, vanilla and milk.
Grill up the pancakes on the preheated griddle.
Top with warmed apple butter and serve.

recipes.title: Healthy Apple Wheat Pancakes
recipes.source_note: Digital cookbook (Kindle)
recipes.description: Whole wheat pancakes with fresh apples and honey, served with sugar-free jam.

instructions.text: Preheat a griddle or skillet.
In a medium bowl, combine the flour, baking powder and salt.
In another bowl whisk together the eggs and honey.
Add the vegetable oil, applesauce, cinnamon and milk.
Stir together the wet ingredients with the dry ingredients.
Fold in the apples.
Grill the pancakes and serve immediately with sugar free jam.

recipes.title: Citrus Blueberry Pancakes
recipes.source_note: Digital cookbook (Kindle)

instructions.text: Combine all ingredients in a medium bowl and whisk together.
Preheat a skillet and coat with cooking spray.
Cook pancakes and serve hot with your favorite syrup.

recipes.title: Apple Ginger Pancakes
recipes.source_note: Digital cookbook (Kindle)

instructions.text: Preheat a non-stick griddle.
Combine batter ingredients and cook pancakes. Serve immediately.

recipes.title: Old Fashioned Belgium Waffles
recipes.source_note: Digital cookbook (Kindle)

instructions.text: Mix all ingredients together.
Cook on a lightly greased Belgium waffle maker for about 5 to 8 minutes.
Serve hot with butter and maple syrup.

recipes.title: Waffles with Summer Berries
recipes.source_note: Digital cookbook (Kindle)

instructions.text: Preheat a waffle maker.
Combine the flour, baking powder, salt, 2 tablespoons of sugar, milk, eggs and butter.
Combine all berries together and mix with remaining 2 tablespoons of sugar; set aside.
Grill the waffles.
Top with sugared berries. Serve immediately.

recipes.title: Peaches and Cream Waffles
recipes.source_note: Digital cookbook (Kindle)

instructions.text: Preheat a griddle.
Combine the flour, baking powder, baking soda, sugar and salt.
Whisk in the eggs, oil and buttermilk.
Fold in the peaches. In another bowl, beat the cream with the vanilla with an electric mixer until peaks form; set aside.
Cook the pancakes. Serve hot with whip cream on the top.

recipes.title: Bananas Foster Waffles
recipes.source_note: Digital cookbook (Kindle)
recipes.description: Light and crunchy waffles topped with sweet banana come together beautifully.

instructions.text: Preheat the waffle iron.
In a large bowl, combine the flour, sugar, salt and baking powder and set aside.
Beat the eggs until fluffy. Add in the butter, milk and vanilla extract. Add the egg mixture to the dry ingredients and beat until smooth.
Ladle the batter into a heated waffle iron that has been sprayed with a non-stick cooking spray. Cook waffles until crisp and golden.

For the topping: In a saucepan, mix butter, sugar, all spice, maple syrup and rum extract (if using). Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until sugar dissolves and the mixture thickens, about 3 to 4 minutes. Add the bananas, coating them with the sauce and cook for a further 3 minutes. Remove from heat.
To serve, spoon the banana mixture over each waffle and garnish with the pecans.

notes: Serving suggestion: Serve with a dollop of whipped cream over the top.

recipes.title: Anise Waffles
recipes.source_note: Digital cookbook (Kindle)
recipes.description: Anise lends a wonderful licorice-like flavor to these unique waffles.

instructions.text: Preheat the waffle iron.
In a large bowl, combine the flour, sugar, salt and baking powder and set aside.
Beat the eggs until fluffy. Add in the butter, milk and anise extract. Add the egg mixture to the dry ingredients and beat until smooth.
Ladle the batter into a heated waffle iron that has been sprayed with a non-stick cooking spray. Cook waffles until crisp and golden.
Serve immediately.

notes: Serving suggestion: Sprinkle with powdered sugar to serve.

recipes.title: Mexican Eggs
recipes.description: Try these when you're in the mood for something a little different.

instructions.text: Beat the eggs. Add the beans and cheese.
Scramble the eggs until done.
Top the eggs with the salsa.

assumptions: Serving size inferred from breakfast category

recipes.title: Huevos Rancheros
recipes.description: Spice up your breakfast with this great south-of-border dish.

instructions.text: Toast the tortillas by placing each one in a skillet on medium heat. Cook both sides for 30 seconds. The tortilla should be soft.
Place the tortillas on a platter.
Melt the butter in a skillet.
Beat the eggs, salt and milk in a bowl. Cook in the skillet.
Transfer two warm tortillas on each plate and divide the scrambled eggs between them.

notes: Serve with the following: Chopped scallions and/or tomatoes, Finely grated cheese, Chopped peppers, Salsa, Guacamole

recipes.title: Texas Eggs
recipes.description: This is perfect for those who love it hot!

instructions.text: Heat up the salsa in a skillet.
Crack the eggs on top of the salsa. Season to taste.
Transfer the salsa and eggs to individual dinner plates.
Serve with the tortilla chips, sour cream, avocado, and cilantro.

assumptions: Serving size inferred from breakfast category

recipes.title: Polenta and Eggs
recipes.description: Polenta is so creamy, and the eggs just add to the flavor.

instructions.text: Place the dried tomatoes in some boiling water and let soak.
Heat up the milk and broth in a saucepan. Add the cornmeal and keep whisking.
Have heat on medium and stir several times for about 15 minutes.
Add the Parmesan and blend. Let sit over low heat.
Remove the dried tomatoes from the water and drain them.
Heat the oil in a skillet. Toss in dried tomatoes and onions. Cook until onions are softened, then take off stove.
Use a deep pan and fill it halfway with water. Squeeze in the juice of the lemon.
When water is simmering, crack the eggs and transfer them carefully into the pan. Let the eggs simmer for 4 minutes, then removed and drain on a paper towel.
Transfer the polenta into individual serving dishes. Top each dish with 2 eggs.

assumptions: Serving size inferred from breakfast category

recipes.title: Johnnycakes
recipes.description: Make enough of these because people will gobble them up.

instructions.text: Mix the cornmeal and the salt.
Warm up the milk and water. Pour into cornmeal mix.
Butter a skillet and a tablespoon to drop the batter.
Fry the johnnycakes until browned on both sides.
Serve with applesauce or butter.

recipes.title: Chocolate Waffle
recipes.description: Waffles are a Sunday treat that everyone loves.

instructions.text: Preheat a waffle iron.
Mix together the flour, cocoa, baking powder, and salt.
Use another bowl to beat the eggs, vanilla, and butter. Add the buttermilk and mix.
Mix in the chocolate chips and combine.
Let batter sit for 10 minutes.
Spray the waffle iron with vegetable spray.
Transfer batter to waffle iron.
Cook until waffles are golden brown on each side.
Repeat with all of the batter. Keep the waffles warm.

assumptions: Serving size inferred from breakfast category

recipes.title: Sausage Twist
recipes.description: This twist can be cut into individual pieces for a yummy breakfast.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees.
Flatten out the dough on a baking sheet.
Top the dough with the sausage, olives and cheeses.
Fold the dough over the filling and make diagonal cuts on top.
Beat the egg and brush over the dough.
Bake for 20 minutes. Dough should be a light brown.
Slice the dough into six portions.

recipes.title: Stuffed French Toast
recipes.description: French toast with a filling – yummy.

instructions.text: Blend the eggs, milk, and honey in a bowl.
Place half of the bread on the bottom of a 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Top with the cream cheese, and the remaining bread.
Top the bread with the egg mixture, making sure to coat all, and chill overnight.
Bake at 350 degrees for 35 minutes.
Top with butter or syrup.

assumptions: Serving size inferred from breakfast category

recipes.title: Sausage and Cheese Breakfast Pizza
recipes.description: Pizza for breakfast - a great way to start the day!

instructions.text: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Brown the sausage over medium heat and drain.

Press the dough together into a greased 12-inch pizza pan to make one round crust. Spread the cooked sausage and bell pepper over the dough and then top evenly with the hash browns. Sprinkle with the cheddar cheese.
Beat together the milk, eggs, salt and pepper until well combined and pour this over the top of the cheddar cheese.
Sprinkle with the Parmesan cheese.
Bake until the crust is browned and cheese is melted, about 25 minutes.

notes: Serving suggestion: For a healthier option, use ground turkey instead of sausage.

assumptions: Serving size inferred from breakfast category

recipes.title: Ham and Cheese Muffins
recipes.description: Delicious and easy to prepare, these are great for breakfast or even lunch on the go.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400°F.
In a large bowl, sift together the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt. Set aside.

In another bowl, beat the egg and add the milk and butter. Mix in the cheese. Pour into the bowl with the dry ingredients and mix quickly to combine, about 10 seconds. Fold in the ham. Do not over mix.
Pour the batter into paper lined muffin pan cups or a greased muffin pan can be used instead.
Bake until the tops are golden, about 20 minutes.

notes: Serving suggestion: The ham can be replaced with crumbled bacon.

recipes.title: Breakfast Tacos
recipes.description: These delicious tacos make a hearty breakfast.

instructions.text: Crumble the sausage into a nonstick pan and cook over medium heat until browned. Set aside.

Whisk the eggs, milk, salt and pepper together. Add the eggs to a lightly greased pan over medium heat. Stir and cook until the eggs are almost firm and then add in the sausage. Continue cooking until eggs are firm.
Heat the tortillas on a griddle. Sprinkle with cheese and spoon in some of the egg and sausage mix. Add salsa and cilantro to your taste.

notes: Serving suggestion: Bacon can be used instead of chorizo.

assumptions: Serving size inferred from breakfast category

recipes.title: Breakfast Parfait
recipes.description: These delicious parfaits can be made ahead and refrigerated for a quick breakfast.

instructions.text: Mix the frozen berries together with the apple juice and vanilla extract. Set aside until the berries are thawed.

Spoon 2 tablespoons of the muesli into four small dishes or glasses. Top each layer of muesli with 2 tablespoons of yoghurt and two tablespoons of the berries. Repeat the layers until all the mix is used up.
Cover and refrigerate until needed.

notes: Serving suggestion: Any of your favorite fruit can be used instead of the frozen berries.

recipes.title: Breakfast Quinoa
recipes.description: Try this breakfast quinoa, packed with fiber and protein, as a great alternative to your morning oatmeal.

instructions.text: Rinse the quinoa until the water runs clear. Strain well.
Heat the milk over medium heat until just warm. Add the quinoa and salt and mix well.
Lower the heat and stir in the cinnamon.
Keep cooking until all the liquid is absorbed by the quinoa, about 20 minutes.
Turn off the heat and mix in the maple syrup.
Fold in the berries, coconut and sunflower seeds and cover and let stand for 5 minutes before serving.

notes: Serving suggestion: More milk can be added for a thinner consistency.

assumptions: Serving size inferred from breakfast category

recipes.title: Breakfast Calzone
recipes.description: A hearty breakfast that can be made ahead and frozen for the week.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Beat 8 eggs with the milk, salt and pepper. Set aside.
In a pan over medium heat cook the sausage until browned. Remove from the pan and drain on paper towels.

Turn heat down to low and cook the eggs, stirring until set. Add the eggs to a bowl together with the pork sausage. Mix them together and allow to cool slightly for about 10 minutes. Then stir in the cheese.

Roll out the dough and divide into 6 rectangles. Divide the egg and sausage mix between them. Fold the dough over and seal the edges with egg wash. Press the tines of a fork all around the edges to seal.
Place calzones on a greased cookie sheet. Brush the remaining egg over the tops and poke once with a fork to create four holes.
Bake until golden brown, about 30 minutes.

notes: Serving suggestion: If preferred, bacon or ham can be used instead of the sausage.

recipes.title: French Toast Casserole
recipes.description: Prepare this delicious treat the night before and simply pop in the oven for a no fuss breakfast.

instructions.text: Grease a 7x11-inch baking dish and fill the bottom with the bread cubes.
Mix together the maple syrup, butter and cream cheese until well combined.
Spoon this mixture evenly over the bread.
Beat together the eggs, half and half, cinnamon, nutmeg and vanilla and pour this mixture over the bread, making sure that all the bread is covered.
Cover with plastic wrap and chill overnight.
The next morning, remove from the fridge and let stand for at least 20 minutes before baking. In the meanwhile, preheat the oven to 350°F.
Bake for an hour or until a toothpick inserted in the middle comes out clean.
Dust with powdered sugar and serve immediately.

notes: Serving suggestion: Serve warm, drizzled with maple syrup.

assumptions: Serving size inferred from breakfast category

recipes.title: Egg and Cheese Frittata
recipes.description: A quick and easy breakfast frittata recipe that can easily be adapted to your taste.

instructions.text: Preheat the oven broiler.
Heat the olive oil in an ovenproof skillet over medium heat.
Beat the eggs with the salt, pepper, garlic powder and scallions and pour into the skillet.
Sprinkle the cheese evenly over the top and place under the broiler until the cheese is melted and the eggs are lightly browned.
Cut into wedges and serve immediately.

notes: Serving suggestion: Add crumbled bacon or ham to your egg mixture for an all-in-one breakfast.

recipes.title: Cheesy Eggs and Spinach Skillet Bake
recipes.description: An easy frittata recipe that can be served for breakfast or paired with a salad for lunch or dinner.

instructions.text: Preheat the oven broiler.
Heat the olive oil in an ovenproof skillet over medium heat.
Beat the eggs with the salt, pepper and garlic powder and pour into the skillet. Layer the spinach over the egg mixture.
Sprinkle the cheese evenly over the top and place under the broiler until the cheese is melted and the eggs are lightly browned.
Cut into wedges and serve immediately.

notes: Serving suggestion: Feta cheese pairs really well with spinach, try using it instead of cheddar in this recipe.

recipes.title: Basic Flapjacks

instructions.text: Sift together flour, sugar, baking powder and salt. Set aside.
Whisk together milk, eggs, butter, and vanilla extract. Gradually add sifted ingredients to milk mixture and whisk until just combined.

Brush a non-stick pan with vegetable oil or melted butter and place over medium heat. Pour about 1/4 cup batter into pan and cook cake until bubbles appear on the surface and underside is slightly browned. Turn flapjack over to cook the other side. Transfer to a heat proof plate and keep warm in a low-heat oven. Repeat with remaining batter.

notes: Serving suggestion: Serve flapjacks with your choice of syrup and fruits.

recipes.title: Traditional Hotcakes

instructions.text: Place water in a kettle and allow to boil. When water is on a full rolling boil, remove from heat and measure one cupful.
Combine cornmeal and salt in a bowl. Gradually add boiling water to cornmeal and stir until you get a thick, pasty mash.
Pour about 4 tablespoons bacon grease or melted butter into a heavy skillet and place over medium heat.
Shape about 1/4 cup of mash into a patty fry one side until brown and crispy. Flip cake to cook the other side. Repeat with remaining mixture.

notes: Serving suggestion: Serve with maple syrup or molasses for breakfast or snacks, or as side dish to mess o' greens.

recipes.title: Breakfast Churros

instructions.text: Combine flour and baking powder in a large bowl. Set aside.

In a medium-sized pan, combine water, canola oil, salt and sugar. Place over medium heat and allow to boil. Remove from heat and gradually add to dry ingredients, stirring as you go. Batter should be sticky and smooth, almost like a dough. Spoon into a pastry bag and set aside.

Pour enough vegetable in a deep pan to fry churros. Oil should be about 2 inches deep. When oil is about 350°F, carefully squeeze churros dough into hot oil, creating an elongated shape. Deep-fry until golden brown. Remove from oil and drain on paper towels. Keep warm in an oven. Repeat with remaining dough.
Cut pastries into desired lengths and sprinkle with granulated sugar or drizzle with honey.

notes: Serving suggestion: Serve with black coffee or hot chocolate. You can pair this with the "Mexican Breakfast Choco Drink" recipe.

recipes.title: Chocolate Chip Porridge

instructions.text: Cook oats and milk over medium-low heat until thick, about 5 minutes, stirring constantly. Divide into 2 bowls and sprinkle with chocolate chips. Drizzle with honey. Sprinkle with cinnamon, if desired. Serve hot.

notes: Serving suggestion: Top porridge with slices of fruit. Serve with orange juice.

recipes.title: Fruity Latvian Breakfast

instructions.text: Mash bananas with grapefruit juice until pasty. Add grapefruit pulp and remaining juice. Stir in wheat germ and linseeds. Transfer to individual bowls and top with boiling water until desired consistency is reached. Sweeten with honey to taste. Serve right away.

notes: Serving suggestion: Replace grapefruit with pineapple (and pineapple juice), or apples (and apple cider). If using apples, blanch apples, peel skin with a vegetable peeler, remove core and chop coarsely. Soak in water until needed to prevent discoloration. Use apple cider instead of grapefruit juice.

recipes.title: Ham and Cheese Open-Faced Sandwiches

instructions.text: Melt butter in a non-stick pan. Combine eggs, chives, water, salt and pepper. Cook, stirring gently, until eggs are slightly set.

Spread filling over each half of the ciabatta. Top with slices of ham, 3 strips of bacon, tomatoes and grated cheese. Arrange on a baking sheet and broil until cheese melts, about 2 to 3 minutes. Serve immediately.

notes: Serving suggestion: Use white bread with crusts trimmed, if ciabatta is not available.

recipes.title: Salmon and Rocket Sandwich
recipes.description: A tasty breakfast sandwich with smoked salmon, bacon, and fresh rocket.

instructions.text: Slice ciabatta lengthwise and toast until crisp.
Arrange smoked salmon slices on the base of bread and spread with cream cheese.
Top with bacon. Season with freshly ground black or cayenne pepper.
Arrange rocket leaves over bacon and cover with other half of ciabatta.
Cut crosswise and serve immediately.

notes: Replace salmon and bacon with your choice of cold cuts, replace rocket with other salad greens.

recipes.title: Spicy Breakfast Migas
recipes.description: A Tex-Mex breakfast dish with crispy tortillas and scrambled eggs.

instructions.text: Fry flour tortillas in oil over high heat until golden and crispy, about 2 to 3 minutes. Drain on paper towels and cut into cubes. If tortillas crumble, that's fine. Save the crumbs as well. Set aside.
Whisk together eggs and half and half with seasonings as desired. Set aside.
Heat canola oil in large pan over medium heat. Sauté red onion until wilted, about 3 minutes.
Add red and green peppers and continue sautéing. Add tomatoes, and stir until tender but not soggy. Add jalapeño and stir a little.
Reduce heat to low and gradually pour in beaten egg mixture. Gently fold eggs into sautéed vegetables until set but not dry.
Sprinkle with cheese and cilantro and cook for another minute. Transfer to a serving plate. Serve warm.

notes: Omit jalapeño, if desired. Use other herbs you prefer.

recipes.title: Southern Grits
recipes.description: Classic Southern-style cheesy grits.

instructions.text: Pour water and salt in a pan. Place over medium heat and boil.
Gradually stir in grits and cook for 1 minute with constant stirring.
Reduce heat to low when mixture starts to boil. Cook for 10 to 15 minutes, stirring frequently.
Remove from heat. Stir in pepper, butter and cheese until melted.

notes: Grits can be served with bacon or sausage, eggs, biscuits or toast.

recipes.title: Bacon and Tomato Frittata
recipes.description: A satisfying, hearty breakfast that is quick and easy to prepare.

instructions.text: Preheat the oven broiler.
Heat the olive oil in an ovenproof skillet over medium heat.
Beat the eggs with the salt, pepper and garlic powder. Mix in the bacon and scallions and pour into the skillet. Layer with the tomato slices.
Sprinkle the cheese evenly over the top and place under the broiler until the cheese is melted and the eggs are lightly browned.
Cut into wedges and serve immediately.

notes: Sprinkle with chopped parsley to serve.
Serve with a green salad for a light lunch or dinner.

recipes.title: Broccoli and Cheese Frittata
recipes.description: An easy to follow frittata recipe that is sure to be a crowd pleaser.

instructions.text: Preheat the oven broiler.
Heat the olive oil in an ovenproof skillet over medium heat. Add the broccoli and cook for 2 minutes.
Beat the eggs with the salt, pepper, garlic powder and scallions and pour over the broccoli.
Sprinkle the cheese evenly over the top and place under the broiler until the cheese is melted and the eggs are lightly browned.
Cut into wedges and serve immediately.

notes: Store leftovers in the fridge and reheat in the microwave before serving.

recipes.title: Cherry Chocolate Scones
recipes.description: These scones make a tasty breakfast treat.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F. Grease a baking sheet and set aside.
Sift the flour and salt together in a large bowl. Rub in the butter. Mix in the chocolate and cherries.
Add the sugar, then milk and egg and combine to get a soft dough.
Knead the dough briefly on a lightly floured surface then roll out into a 1/2-inch thick round.
Divide and cut into 8 wedges, and place on the prepared baking sheet.
Bake for 15 minutes or until golden brown.

notes: If preferred, white chocolate chips can be used instead of the semi-sweet chocolate.

recipes.title: Apricot Scones
recipes.description: A delicious treat to go with your morning coffee.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F. Grease a baking sheet and set aside.
Sift the flour, cinnamon and salt together in a large bowl. Rub in the butter. Mix in the apricots.
Add the sugar, then milk and egg and combine to get a soft dough.
Knead the dough briefly on a lightly floured surface then roll out into a 1/2-inch thick round.
Divide and cut into 8 wedges, and place on the prepared baking sheet.
Bake for 15 minutes or until golden brown.

notes: Store leftovers in an airtight container for up to three days.

recipes.title: Cinnamon Oat Scones
recipes.description: A delicious lightly spiced scone. Serve for breakfast or as a teatime treat.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F. Grease a baking sheet and set aside.
Mix the flours, oats, cinnamon and salt together in a large bowl. Rub in the butter.
Add the sugar, then milk, egg and maple syrup and combine to get a soft dough.
Knead the dough briefly on a lightly floured surface then roll out into a 1/2-inch thick round.
Divide and cut into 8 wedges, and place on the prepared baking sheet.
Bake for 20 minutes or until golden brown.

notes: Add a handful of raisins to the dough if desired.

recipes.title: Pumpkin Chocolate Chip Scones
recipes.description: Pumpkin and chocolate pair beautifully together in this delicious scone.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Whisk together the flour, sugar, spices, baking powder, baking soda and salt.
Blend the butter into the flour mixture slowly, using two knives or working with your fingers, until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs. Set aside.
In another bowl, combine the buttermilk, pumpkin puree, chocolate chips and vanilla and mix well. Add this to the dry ingredients and mix till dough is formed.
On a floured surface, gently knead the dough five or six times and pat into a circle that is about one and a half inches thick and seven inches wide.
Cut this circle into quarters, and then each quarter in half so you have eight scones. Beat the egg and milk together and brush over the tops of the scones.
Bake for 15 minutes or until an inserted toothpick comes out clean. Transfer to a wire rack and cool.

notes: Drizzle with chocolate syrup before serving.

recipes.title: Apple Cheddar Muffins
recipes.description: Cheddar and apple go well together in this tasty breakfast muffin.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400°F.
In a large bowl, sift together the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt. Set aside.
In another bowl, beat the egg and add the milk and butter. Pour into the bowl with the dry ingredients and mix quickly to combine, about 10 seconds. Fold in the apple and cheese. Do not over mix.
Pour the batter into paper lined muffin pan cups or a greased muffin pan can be used instead.
Bake until the tops are golden, about 20 minutes.

notes: Serve warm with apple butter.

recipes.title: Banana Cinnamon Muffins
recipes.description: Delicious and moist to the last bite, these muffins will disappear quickly.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400°F.
In a large bowl, sift together the flour, baking powder, sugar, cinnamon and salt. Set aside.
In another bowl, beat the egg and add the milk, butter, banana and vanilla. Pour into the bowl with the dry ingredients and mix quickly to combine, about 10 seconds.
Pour the batter into paper lined muffin pan cups or a greased muffin pan can be used instead.
Bake until the tops are golden, about 20 minutes.

notes: Serve warm, drizzled with honey.

recipes.title: Raisin Bran Muffins
recipes.description: Delicious breakfast muffins that are a great source of fiber.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400°F.
In a large bowl, sift together the flour, wheat bran, baking powder, sugar, cinnamon and salt. Mix in the raisins. Set aside.
In another bowl, beat the egg and add the milk, butter and vanilla. Pour into the bowl with the dry ingredients and mix quickly to combine, about 10 seconds.
Pour the batter into paper lined muffin pan cups or a greased muffin pan can be used instead.
Bake until the tops are golden, about 20 minutes.

notes: Serve warm with butter.

recipes.title: Raspberry Cheesecake Poppy Seed Muffins
recipes.description: Cream cheese and tart raspberries are a great match in these delicious, moist muffins.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400°F.
In a large bowl, sift together the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt. Set aside.

In another bowl, beat the egg and add the milk, butter, cream cheese, poppy seeds and vanilla. Pour into the bowl with the dry ingredients and mix quickly to combine, about 10 seconds. Fold in the raspberries.
Pour the batter into paper lined muffin pan cups or a greased muffin pan can be used instead.
Bake until the tops are golden, about 20 minutes.

notes: Use half a cup of chopped walnuts instead of poppy seeds if desired.

recipes.title: Cinnamon and Spice Muffins
recipes.description: These spiced muffins are great for breakfast, teatime or just a snack on the go.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400°F.
In a large bowl, sift together the flour, baking powder, sugar, spices and salt. Set aside.
In another bowl, beat the egg and add the milk, butter and vanilla. Pour into the bowl with the dry ingredients and mix quickly to combine, about 10 seconds. Do not beat the mixture.
Pour the batter into paper lined muffin pan cups or a greased muffin pan can be used instead.
Bake until the tops are golden, about 20 minutes.

notes: Add half a cup of your favorite nuts to the batter before baking.

recipes.title: Nutella Muffins
recipes.description: Deliciously moist to the last bite, these muffins are sure to disappear quickly.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400°F.
In a large bowl, sift together the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt. Set aside.
In another bowl, beat the egg and add the milk, butter and Nutella. Pour into the bowl with the dry ingredients and mix quickly to combine, about 10 seconds. Do not beat the mixture.
Pour the batter into paper lined muffin pan cups or a greased muffin pan can be used instead.
Bake until the tops are golden, about 20 minutes.

notes: If desired, add 1/4 cup of chopped walnuts to the batter before baking.

assumptions: Serving size inferred from breakfast category

recipes.title: Eggnog Muffins
recipes.description: These lightly spiced eggnog muffins are a great holiday treat.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400°F.
In a large bowl, sift together the flour, baking powder, sugar, spices and salt. Set aside.
In another bowl, beat the egg and add the milk, butter, eggnog and vanilla. Pour into the bowl with the dry ingredients and mix quickly to combine, about 10 seconds. Do not beat the mixture.
Pour the batter into paper lined muffin pan cups or a greased muffin pan can be used instead.
Bake until the tops are golden, about 20 minutes.

notes: These muffins freeze well, just pop in the microwave for a couple minutes before serving.

recipes.title: Coconut Muffins
recipes.description: Definitely for coconut lovers - this light, moist muffin is sure to be a crowd pleaser.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400°F.
In a large bowl, sift together the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt. Set aside.

In another bowl, beat the egg and add the milk, butter and vanilla. Mix in the coconut. Pour into the bowl with the dry ingredients and mix quickly to combine, about 10 seconds. Do not beat the mixture.
Pour the batter into paper lined muffin pan cups or a greased muffin pan can be used instead.
Bake until the tops are golden, about 20 minutes.

recipes.title: Hash Brown Frittata
recipes.description: A filling frittata recipe that can be made for breakfast, lunch or dinner.

instructions.text: Preheat the oven broiler.
Heat the olive oil in a large ovenproof skillet over medium heat. Add the hash brown potatoes to the skillet and cook for 10 minutes.
Beat the eggs with the salt, pepper and garlic powder and pour into the skillet over the hash browns. Layer the spinach over the egg mixture.
Sprinkle the cheese evenly over the top and place under the broiler until the cheese is melted and the eggs are lightly browned.
Cut into wedges and serve immediately.

assumptions: Serving size inferred from breakfast category

recipes.title: Gingerbread Waffles
recipes.description: With wonderful warm spices, this seasonal waffle recipe is great for the festive season.

instructions.text: Preheat the waffle iron.
In a large bowl, combine the flour, sugar, salt, spices and baking powder and set aside.
Beat the eggs until fluffy. Add in the butter, milk and molasses. Add the egg mixture to the dry ingredients and beat until smooth.
Ladle the batter into a heated waffle iron that has been sprayed with a non-stick cooking spray. Cook waffles until crisp and golden.
Serve immediately.

notes: Top with whipped cream and drizzle with molasses.

recipes.title: Norwegian Waffles
recipes.description: Deliciously light and fluffy waffles that are so easy to whip up.

instructions.text: Preheat the waffle iron.
In a large bowl, combine the flour, sugar, salt and baking powder and set aside.
Beat the eggs until fluffy. Add in the butter, milk and vanilla extract. Add the egg mixture to the dry ingredients and beat until smooth. Let the batter set for half an hour before cooking.
Ladle the batter into a heated waffle iron that has been sprayed with a non-stick cooking spray. Cook waffles until crisp and golden.
Serve immediately.

notes: Spread with sour cream and jam to serve.

recipes.title: Cornmeal Waffles
recipes.description: These savory waffles are great served with a bowl of stew, chili or soup.

instructions.text: Preheat the waffle iron.
In a large bowl, combine the flour, cornmeal, sugar, salt and baking powder and set aside.
Beat the eggs until fluffy. Add in the butter, milk and vanilla extract. Add the egg mixture to the dry ingredients and beat until smooth.
Ladle the batter into a heated waffle iron that has been sprayed with a non-stick cooking spray. Cook waffles until crisp and golden.
Serve immediately.

notes: Garnish with sour cream and shredded cheddar cheese, serve with a bowl of chili.

recipes.title: Banana Waffles
recipes.description: These waffles are great as a snack, breakfast or dessert.

instructions.text: Preheat the waffle iron.
In a large bowl, combine the flour, sugar, cinnamon, salt and baking powder and set aside.
Beat the eggs until fluffy. Add in the butter, milk, banana and vanilla extract. Add the egg mixture to the dry ingredients and beat until smooth.
Ladle the batter into a heated waffle iron that has been sprayed with a non-stick cooking spray. Cook waffles until crisp and golden.
Serve immediately.

notes: For a healthier option substitute half of the all-purpose flour with whole-wheat flour.

assumptions: Serving size inferred from breakfast category

recipes.title: German Pancakes
recipes.description: Oven-baked puffy pancakes with lemon and powdered sugar.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Place shortening in a large cast iron skillet and place in oven for about 7 minutes.
In a medium bowl, combine the flour, salt and sugar.
In another bowl, bring together the butter, eggs, milk and vanilla. Add the juice and zest of one lemon.
Place batter in greased skillet and bake for about 20-25 minutes, until the pancake puffs up.
Remove from oven and loosen the pancake with a spatula.
Place the pancake on a large plate. Dust with powdered sugar, lemon juice and lemon zest. Serve immediately.

recipes.source_note: Recipe Keeper App

recipes.title: Oven Apple Pancakes
recipes.description: A great hassle-free pancake breakfast baked in the oven.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Add the butter to a 13x9-inch ovenproof dish and place in the oven until the butter melts. Remove the dish from the oven and swirl the butter around so that the entire base of the dish is coated.
Add the apples to the dish, spreading them out evenly. Sprinkle with the brown sugar and bake until the apple slices start to soften slightly, about ten minutes.
Meanwhile, in a large bowl whisk together the milk, eggs, sugar, vanilla and salt. Add the flour and keep whisking until the batter is smooth.
Pour the batter over the apples and bake for a further 20 minutes, until the pancake is puffed and golden brown.
Serve immediately.

notes: Serve with syrup and sprinkle with powdered sugar.
recipes.source_note: Recipe Keeper App

recipes.title: Egg Chops
recipes.source_note: Many Ways for Cooking Eggs (Project Gutenberg, public domain)
recipes.description: Vintage recipe

instructions.text: Chop the eggs very fine, mix them with the ham; add the parsley, onion juice and pepper. Rub the butter and flour together and add the milk. Stir until you have a smooth, thick sauce, then add the salt; mix this with the other ingredients and turn it out to cool. When cold form into a chop about the size of an ordinary mutton chop. Dip first in egg beaten with a tablespoonful of water, then cover carefully with bread crumbs and fry in deep hot fat. Serve with either tomato or brown sauce.

recipes.title: Eggs Scrambled With Fresh Tomatoes
recipes.source_note: Many Ways for Cooking Eggs (Project Gutenberg, public domain)
recipes.description: Vintage recipe

instructions.text: Peel the tomatoes, cut them into halves and squeeze out the seeds. Cut the tomatoes into small bits, put them into a saucepan with the salt, pepper and butter; when these are hot add the eggs, beaten until well mixed, stir until the eggs are "set," turn into a heated dish, garnish with toast and send to the table.

recipes.title: Scrambled Eggs With Asparagus Tips
recipes.source_note: Many Ways for Cooking Eggs (Project Gutenberg, public domain)
recipes.description: Vintage recipe

instructions.text: Beat the eggs, add the salt, pepper and butter. Put them into a saucepan, add at once the asparagus tips and stir with a fork until the mixture is "set."

recipes.title: Omelet With Potatoes
recipes.source_note: Many Ways for Cooking Eggs (Project Gutenberg, public domain)
recipes.description: Vintage recipe

instructions.text: Beat the eggs, without separating, until thoroughly mixed; add them gradually to the mashed potato, beating all the while; add the salt and pepper. Put the butter into a good-sized saute or omelet pan; when hot, turn the ingredients into the pan, and smooth it down with a pallet knife. Let this cook slowly until nicely browned; fold it over as you would a plain omelet, and turn onto a heated dish. The parsley may be sprinkled over the top, or added to the mixture.

recipes.title: Omelet A La Duchesse
recipes.source_note: Many Ways for Cooking Eggs (Project Gutenberg, public domain)
recipes.description: Vintage recipe

ingredients.item: ful of vanilla or orange flower water

instructions.text: This is a sweet baked omelet, and is served the same as one would serve an omelet souffle.

Put the sugar, water, cinnamon and lemon rind over the fire, boil until it spins a thread and stand aside to cool. Separate the eggs; beat the yolks until creamy, and add the cream, then the strained syrup. Add the vanilla, and when cool fold in the well-beaten whites. Turn at once into a shallow silver or granite dish, dust thickly with powdered sugar and bake in a quick oven until brown.

recipes.title: Brioche French Toast
recipes.source_note: Hell's Kitchen Cookbook, page 126
recipes.description: Thick brioche bread dipped in vanilla-ginger custard and pan-fried, perfect as a base for foie gras.

ingredients.prep_note: seed scraped, or 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract

instructions.text: Preheat the oven to 200°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Cut the slices of bread in half.
In a shallow bowl, whisk together the eggs, vanilla, ginger, and cream.
Heat the grapeseed oil in a nonstick sauté pan over medium heat.
Dip the brioche in the egg mixture, then add it to the pan and cook 2 minutes on the first side, then flip and cook 1 more minute.
Transfer the French toast to the lined baking sheet and place in the oven to keep warm.

recipes.title: Spicy Heavy Cream Eggs
recipes.source_note: Food My Muse (foodmymuse.com)
recipes.description: Eggs fried in caramelized heavy cream with salsa macha, creating a creamy sauce similar to browned butter.

instructions.text: Preheat a pan for 2 minutes on high. Add heavy cream and salsa macha, lower heat to medium, and simmer for 1 minute.
Add eggs and cover. Cook for 2-3 minutes until the whites set.
Top with chives and additional salsa macha.

tips: Make sure you let the heavy cream and salsa macha caramelize.

recipes.title: Tomato Pesto Eggs
recipes.source_note: Food My Muse (foodmymuse.com)
recipes.description: Eggs cooked in caramelized heavy cream with homemade pesto rosso made from sun-dried tomatoes, pine nuts, and Parmigiano Reggiano.

ingredients.prep_note: plus more for topping; see below for homemade

ingredients.item: sun-dried tomatoes packed in olive oil

instructions.text: Separate oil from sun-dried tomatoes. Add tomatoes, pine nuts, Parmigiano, garlic, and basil to a food processor. Process until chunky, add tomato oil, then process again. Season with salt, pepper, and additional olive oil as desired.
Bring heavy cream to a simmer, add pesto rosso, and return to medium-high heat. Once edges begin caramelizing slightly, add eggs.
Cook eggs on medium for 2 minutes, then cover and cook another 2 minutes until set.
Serve with additional pesto, basil, and black pepper.

tips: Make sure you let the cream caramelize.

assumptions: Nutrition as provided by source website

recipes.title: French Eggs
recipes.source_note: Food My Muse (foodmymuse.com)
recipes.description: Eggs baked over toasted crusty bread and ham with heavy cream, nutmeg, and melted Gruyère cheese.

instructions.text: Preheat pan on high for 2 minutes. Lower heat to medium, add butter and bread. Toast for about 5 minutes until golden.
Add ham and sauté for 2-3 minutes. Make a well in the center and add cream and nutmeg. Caramelize for about 3 minutes. Add cheese to pan edges and eggs in the center.
Cook covered until eggs are set. Top with black pepper, salt, and chives.

tips: Make sure you cover the bread with the béchamel entirely.

recipes.title: Heavy Cream Scrambled Eggs
recipes.source_note: Food My Muse (foodmymuse.com)
recipes.description: Scrambled eggs cooked in caramelized heavy cream with salsa macha for rich, large-curd eggs.

instructions.text: Whisk eggs and strain them.
Preheat pan for 2 minutes on medium-high heat. Add cream and caramelize on medium for 2-3 minutes.
Add salsa macha and the eggs to the pan.
Let eggs barely set, then add salt and pepper. Gently move them around to create large curds.
Divide into plates, top with additional salsa macha and generous amounts of chives.

tips: Make sure you let the cream caramelize for the best flavor development.
Strain whisked eggs for a smoother texture.

assumptions: Nutrition as provided by source website

recipes.title: Turkish Eggs
recipes.source_note: Food My Muse (foodmymuse.com)
recipes.description: Poached eggs served over herbed labneh and drenched in spiced brown butter with chipotle, smoked paprika, and salsa macha.

instructions.text: Mix labneh with lemon zest, salt, cilantro, dill, garlic, and chives in a bowl.
Melt butter in a saucepan until golden and nutty. Add chipotle powder, smoked paprika, salsa macha, and sesame seeds. Pour into a separate bowl, leaving some butter in the pan.
Toast bread slices in the remaining butter in the saucepan.
Strain eggs to remove watery whites. Bring water to a simmer and create a whirlpool effect. Poach eggs for 1 1/2 to 2 minutes for runny yolks.
Spoon labneh onto a plate, top with poached eggs, and drench in spiced brown butter. Garnish with za'atar, cilantro, dill, and chives. Serve with toasted bread.

tips: For better poaching results, soak eggs in a 2:1 water/apple cider vinegar mixture for about 30 minutes to form a protective barrier around the whites.

recipes.title: Spicy Breakfast Tacos
recipes.source_note: https://www.chilipeppermadness.com/recipes/breakfast-tacos/
recipes.description: Loaded with Mexican chorizo, crispy potatoes, scrambled eggs, and jalapeños. The perfect way to start your day!

instructions.text: Cook potatoes in oil until crispy, about 10 minutes. Season with chili powder.
Add jalapeños and onion, cook 3 more minutes. Remove and set aside.
Brown chorizo in the same pan, breaking it up as it cooks.
Push chorizo to the side, scramble eggs in the pan.
Combine eggs, chorizo, and potato mixture.
Fill tortillas with mixture, top with cheese, salsa, and cilantro.

notes: Use small diced potatoes for faster cooking.
Can substitute bacon for chorizo.
Add avocado or sour cream for extra richness.

recipes.title: Migas (Scrambled Eggs with Crispy Tortillas)
recipes.source_note: https://www.chilipeppermadness.com/chili-pepper-recipes/breakfasts/migas/
recipes.description: Traditional Mexican breakfast with scrambled eggs, crispy fried tortilla strips, jalapeños, tomatoes, and melty cheese.

instructions.text: Fry tortilla strips in oil until crispy. Drain on paper towels.
Melt butter in the pan, add onion and jalapeño. Cook 2 minutes.
Add tomato and cook 1 minute.
Pour in beaten eggs and scramble gently.
When eggs are almost set, fold in tortilla strips and cheese.
Season with salt and pepper, garnish with cilantro.
Serve with warm tortillas, salsa, and refried beans.

notes: The crispy tortillas should stay slightly crunchy.
Don't overscramble - eggs should be soft and creamy.
Popular in Texas and Mexico.

recipes.title: Shakshuka
recipes.source_note: https://www.chilipeppermadness.com/recipes/shakshuka/
recipes.description: Popular North African and Middle Eastern dish of eggs poached in spicy tomato sauce, perfect for breakfast or any time.

instructions.text: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Sauté onion and bell pepper until soft.
Add garlic and cook 1 minute.
Add tomatoes, cumin, paprika, cayenne, and salt. Simmer 10 minutes.
Make 6 wells in the sauce. Crack an egg into each well.
Cover and cook 8-10 minutes until egg whites are set but yolks are still runny.
Garnish with herbs and feta. Serve with crusty bread for dipping.

notes: The runny yolk mixed with sauce is the best part.
Add harissa for more heat and authentic flavor.
Serve straight from the skillet.

recipes.title: Blancmange In Eggs.
recipes.source_note: Domestic French Cookery, 4th ed. (Project Gutenberg, public domain)
recipes.description: Vintage recipe

ingredients.item: from the middle of each cupful

instructions.text: Take two ounces of shelled sweet almonds, and one ounce of shelled bitter almonds. Blanch them by throwing them into scalding water to make the skins peel off easily; then put them in cold water; wipe them dry afterwards, and pound them in a mortar, adding at times a little rose-water.

Dissolve an ounce of isinglass in warm water, and then stir it into a quart of cream. Add a quarter of a pound of broken loaf-sugar, and a wine-glass of rose-water. Boil it hard for a quarter of an hour, and stir it all the time. Then strain it through a linen bag, and put it into egg-cups, or into the halves of egg-shells nicely and evenly trimmed, and set it away in a cold place to congeal.

Have ready some calves-feet jelly (made according to the directions given in the article “Chickens in Jelly”); and when the blancmange is firm, take out a small piece from the middle of each cupful, and replace it with a lump of the jelly, put in so as to look like the yolk of the egg. Or if more convenient, you need not put in the jelly[84] till you have taken the blancmange out of the cups or egg-shells, which must be done by wetting the moulds with warm water on the outside.
The jelly for this purpose must be very high-colored, by means of brandy, or dark sweet wine.
If nicely managed, the blancmange and jelly will look like eggs cut in half. Lay them in a circle round a dish that contains something high and ornamental,—for instance, a pyramid of ice-cream.

recipes.title: Boiled Eggs.
recipes.source_note: Domestic French Cookery, 4th ed. (Project Gutenberg, public domain)
recipes.description: Vintage recipe

instructions.text: When the water boils hard, put in the eggs, and let them boil exactly three minutes. Then take them out, and cover them up for about a minute, which will greatly improve them. Send them to table wrapped in a napkin, and laid in a deep dish.

recipes.title: Codfish With Egg Sauce
recipes.source_note: Simple Italian Cookery (Project Gutenberg, public domain)
recipes.description: Vintage recipe

instructions.text: Take one pound of salt codfish. Boil it and remove the skin and bones. Then fry lightly in butter, adding chopped-up parsley, salt, and pepper. Stir about constantly, and add from time to time a little boiling water, until the fish is thoroughly cooked. Then beat up the yolks of two eggs and add them with a little flour, and cook for a few moments more. Squeeze on some lemon juice and serve.

recipes.title: Curried Eggs
recipes.source_note: Many Ways for Cooking Eggs (Project Gutenberg, public domain)
recipes.description: Vintage recipe

instructions.text: Peel, and cut into slices, three large onions. Put them in a saucepan with two tablespoonfuls of butter. Stand over hot water and cook until the onions are soft. Add a teaspoonful of curry powder, a clove of garlic mashed, a saltspoonful of ground ginger, a half teaspoonful of salt and a tablespoonful of flour; mix thoroughly and add a half pint of water. Stir until boiling. Have ready six hard-boiled eggs, cut them into slices, arrange them over a dish of carefully boiled rice, on a hot platter, strain over the sauce, and send at once to the table. This dish is made more attractive by a garnish with sweet Spanish peppers, cut into strips.

recipes.title: Deviled Eggs
recipes.source_note: Many Ways for Cooking Eggs (Project Gutenberg, public domain)
recipes.description: Vintage recipe

instructions.text: Hard-boil twelve eggs. Remove the shells. Cut the eggs into halves, crosswise. Take out the yolks without breaking the whites. Press the yolks through a sieve. Add four tablespoonfuls of finely chopped chicken, tongue or ham. Add a half teaspoonful of salt, a saltspoonful of pepper and two tablespoonfuls of melted butter. Rub the mixture. Form it into balls the size of the yolks and put them into the places in the whites from which the yolks were taken. Put two halves together, roll them in tissue paper that has been fringed at the ends, giving each a twist. If these balls are made the size of the yolk, and put back into the whites, they may be placed on a platter, heated, and served on toast, with cream sauce; then they are very much like the eggs Bernhardt.

recipes.title: Egg Balls
recipes.source_note: Many Ways for Cooking Eggs (Project Gutenberg, public domain)
recipes.description: Vintage Italian recipe

instructions.text: These are used for soup and for garnishing of vegetable dishes. Hard-boil four eggs, throw them at once into cold water, remove the shells. Put the yolks through a sieve, then add a half teaspoonful of salt, a dash of white pepper and the yolk of one raw egg, or you may take a part of the white of one egg. Mix thoroughly and make into balls the size of a marble, using enough flour to prevent sticking to the hands. Drop these into a kettle of boiling stock, or into hot fat. Drain on brown paper.

recipes.title: Egg Croquettes
recipes.source_note: Simple Italian Cookery (Project Gutenberg, public domain)
recipes.description: Vintage Italian recipe

instructions.text: Hard boil two eggs, remove the shells, dry them, and cut the eggs in minute pieces. Put one tablespoon of butter into a saucepan, and when it is melted add one and one-half tablespoons of flour; stir constantly for a few moments over a slow fire with a wooden spoon, taking care that the flour does not color. Then pour in one-third of a cup of milk, in which you have put salt and pepper. Cool this sauce for eight or ten minutes, stirring continually to make it smooth, then remove from the fire, put in the chopped-up egg, some parsley chopped fine, and one-half tablespoon of grated Parmesan cheese. When you have mixed these ingredients well together, spread them out on a plate or marble and allow to cool. When this has become cold and hardened, with a wooden spoon divide it into little portions about the size of a nut. Take these and roll them in dried bread crumbs and a little flour. Roll them all then, one at a time, with a rotary motion, and then elongate the balls until they are the shape of ordinary corks, then dip the croquettes into the egg, one at a time, then into bread crumbs again, and a few moments before serving fry in boiling lard. As soon as they are colored remove them immediately from the lard, otherwise they will break to pieces.
Polenta Fritters, Fried Pumpkin, Fried Squash, and Parsnips may also be added or substituted if desired.
